title: Gradient flow towards quantum states with ideal quantum geometry
abstract: We propose a gradient-flow method for quantum states in lattice models, generated by an action consisting of the quantum-metric and the square of the Berry curvature. These two terms drive the spectral projector toward Bogomolny saturation and uniform Berry curvature, respectively. We show that, due to a no-go theorem for finite-dimensional projectors, the two conditions cannot in general be satisfied simultaneously in lattice models. Hence the flow is expected to approach a nontrivial fixed point that balances the two geometric requirements. For the Wilson-Dirac model, we demonstrate that the flowed projector exhibits almost uniform Berry curvature while remaining close to the Bogomolny bound. We further construct a short-range truncated flattened Hamiltonian from the flowed projector and obtain a lattice model with nearly flat bands and nearly uniform Berry curvature. We also apply the method to the Hofstadter model and confirm the roles of the metric and Berry-curvature terms in a Chern band with higher Chern number.
summary: This paper introduces a gradient-flow technique to optimize quantum states in lattice models towards ideal quantum geometry. By balancing the drive towards Bogomolny saturation and uniform Berry curvature, the method successfully constructs simplified, short-range Hamiltonians. This provides a theoretical pathway for designing materials with desired topological properties like flat bands and uniform Berry curvature.
main_problem: The paper develops a gradient-flow method to drive quantum states in lattice models towards an 'ideal quantum geometry' by simultaneously balancing two competing geometric requirements: Bogomolny saturation and uniform Berry curvature.
main_result: The flow converges to a non-trivial fixed point that balances these two requirements, allowing for the construction of short-range lattice Hamiltonians exhibiting nearly flat bands and uniform Berry curvature.
method: A gradient-flow equation, derived from an action combining the quantum metric and the square of the Berry curvature, is used to evolve the spectral projector on the manifold of quantum states.
model_or_system: The method is tested on lattice models, specifically the Wilson-Dirac model and the Hofstadter model, which are used to study topological properties in condensed matter systems.
key_observables:
Quantum metric ($g_{\mu
u}$), Berry curvature ($\Omega$), Bogomolny defect ($\delta_B$), and the normalized ratios $R_{\Omega}$ and $R_B$.
important_parameters: The flow is controlled by parameters $(\alpha,  eta)$ weighting the metric and curvature terms, respectively.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the combined flow is necessary because the two geometric conditions cannot be satisfied simultaneously in finite-dimensional lattice models (a 'no-go theorem').
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of Berry curvature ($\Omega(k)$) and the dependence of the reduction ratios ($R_{\Omega}$ and $R_B$) on the weighting parameter $ eta$.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the gradient flow formalism and the competing geometric bounds. It then analyzes the flow equations for the metric and curvature, demonstrating the trade-off. Finally, it applies this to specific models (Wilson-Dirac, Hofstadter) to construct improved, short-range Hamiltonians.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, geometric tool for designing effective Hamiltonians for topological materials, which is highly relevant for understanding band structure engineering in condensed matter physics.
